questions.questionText:
A digital stop-clock measures time in minutes and seconds.
The stop-clock reads 00:50 when it is started (i.e. 00 minutes 50 seconds).
It reads 02:10 when it is stopped.
What is the shortest possible time that has passed between starting and stopping the stop-clock?

Four students are instructed to find the time it takes for a ball bearing to fall through a vertical
height of 1.0m.
Each student uses a different procedure.
Which student follows the correct procedure?

options.text: The student measures the time taken for the ball to fall 1.0m five times. He then adds the times taken together and divides by five.
The student measures the time taken for the ball to fall 1.0m five times. He then multiplies the times taken together and divides by five.
The student measures the time taken for the ball to fall 2.0m. He then divides the time taken by two.
The student measures the time taken for the ball to fall 2.0m five times. He then adds the times taken together and divides by ten.

questions.questionText: Which property of an object is a gravitational force acting on its mass?

Which equation is correct?
acceleration
What is meant by the moment of a force?

options.text: the work done by the force
the time for which the force acts
the turning effect of the force

questions.questionText:
A force acts on an area to produce a pressure.
Which changes produce the same pressure?

options.text: doubling the area and doubling the force
doubling the area and halving the force
doubling the area and making the force four times bigger
halving the area and doubling the force

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows a cylinder containing oxygen under high pressure.
The temperature of the cylinder and the oxygen decreases.
Which statement describes what happens to the pressure in the cylinder and gives the reason
why the pressure changes?

options.text: The pressure decreases because the oxygen particles move faster.
The pressure decreases because the oxygen particles move more slowly.
The pressure increases because the oxygen particles move faster.
The pressure increases because the oxygen particles move more slowly.

questions.questionText: Which statement describes what happens during solidification?

options.text: Particles begin to move around each other easily.
Particles stop moving around each other.
The temperature of the particles continues to decrease during solidification.
The temperature of the particles continues to increase during solidification.

questions.questionText:
A girl blows some air into a party balloon and ties a knot to seal the air in the balloon.
The girl holds the sealed balloon above a hot convector heater.
She observes that the volume of the balloon increases significantly.
Which statement identifies the cause of this increase in volume?

options.text: The air in the balloon contracts.
The air in the balloon expands.
The material of the balloon contracts.
The material of the balloon expands.

questions.questionText:
A candle is used to heat some water in a glass beaker.
glass beaker
water
candle
What is the main method of heat transfer through the glass and within the water?
through the glass within the water
Which equation enables the speed of a wave to be calculated?

The diagram shows how a converging lens forms an image of an object.
object
image
Which description of the image formed by the lens is correct?

Which row describes the image viewed in a plane mirror?
type of image image size

The table gives the range of frequencies of three types of electromagnetic radiation.
type of radiation range of frequencies/Hz
radio 3  104 to 3  109
visible light 4  1014 to 8  1014
X-rays 3  1016 to 3  1019
Which type of electromagnetic radiation has a frequency of 4  1015Hz?

A plotting compass is placed close to the pole of a magnet with poles marked X and Y. The
N pole of the plotting compass points to pole X, as shown.
X Y
Pole Y of the magnet is then placed close to another magnet with poles marked P and Q, as
shown. The magnets repel each other.
X Y P Q
magnets repel
Which row is correct?
pole X pole P
Why are electrical cables often made from copper?

options.text: Copper contains free electrons and is a good conductor.
Copper contains free electrons and is a good insulator.
Copper contains free protons and is a good conductor.
Copper contains free protons and is a good insulator.

questions.questionText:
There is a current I in a resistor. The potential difference (p.d.) across the resistor is V.
What does the product IV represent?

options.text: the charge flowing through the resistor
the energy transferred by the resistor
the power dissipated by the resistor

questions.questionText:
An isolated metal sphere is positively charged.
It is then brought near to another isolated metal sphere that is neutral.
left right
+ +
+ +
+ +
positively charged + + + neutral
metal sphere metal sphere
What happens to the charges on the neutral sphere as the positively charged sphere is brought
close to it?

options.text: Some positive charges move to the left and some negative charges move to the right.
Some positive charges move to the right and some negative charges move to the left.
Some positive charges move to the right, but the negative charges do not move.
The positive charges do not move, but some negative charges move to the left.

questions.questionText:
A copper wire rests in a uniform magnetic field.
Which change causes an induced electromotive force (e.m.f.) in the wire?

options.text: connecting the wire to a power supply

An element has two isotopes.
Which row compares the nucleus of one atom of each isotope?
the charge the mass
on each nucleus of each nucleus

In a laboratory, a radiation detector is connected to a counter which shows a reading for the
count rate due to background radiation.
detector
Which unit is count rate measured in?
Which statement about alpha, beta and gamma emissions is correct?

options.text: Beta-particles are not deflected by magnetic fields.
Gamma rays are more penetrating than alpha-particles and beta-particles.
Gamma rays are more ionising than alpha-particles and beta-particles.
